contexts: Leveraged Lending Policy â€” Section 4.1: Leveraged loans are credit facilities to borrowers whose total debt-to-EBITDA ratio including the proposed facility exceeds 4.0x at origination.

Leveraged Lending Policy â€” Section 4.3: Leveraged lending transactions require approval from a senior credit officer. The aggregate leveraged loan portfolio must not exceed 15% of total corporate loan outstandings.

question: What are the requirements for managing risks in securities lending?
ground_truth: Securities lending must be fully collateralised at a minimum of 102% of the market value of lent securities. Collateral must be marked to market daily. Transactions must be governed by master securities lending agreements.
contexts: Securities Lending Policy â€” Section 3.1: All securities lending transactions must be collateralised at a minimum of 102% of the market value of the lent securities, marked to market daily.

Securities Lending Policy â€” Section 3.3: Counterparties must be pre-approved by the Credit Committee. All transactions must be governed by a Master Securities Lending Agreement. Collateral eligibility must comply with the approved collateral schedule.

question: What are the requirements for managing the risk of money market fund investments?
ground_truth: Investments are restricted to VNAV and LVNAV funds rated AAAmmf by at least one NRSRO. No more than 10% of the liquidity portfolio may be held in funds from any single manager.
contexts: Money Market Fund Investment Policy â€” Section 2.1: The firm may only invest in VNAV or LVNAV money market funds carrying a rating of AAAmmf from at least one NRSRO.

Money Market Fund Investment Policy â€” Section 2.3: Investments from any single fund manager must not exceed 10% of the total liquidity portfolio. Funds must be reviewed for continued eligibility quarterly.

question: What are the requirements for managing risks in trade repository reporting?
ground_truth: Reportable OTC derivatives must be reported to an approved trade repository by end of day T+1. Records must be reconciled monthly. Reporting errors must be corrected within 5 business days.
contexts: Trade Repository Reporting Policy â€” Section 4.1: OTC derivatives subject to mandatory reporting must be reported to a registered trade repository by end of day T+1.

Trade Repository Reporting Policy â€” Section 4.3: Records at the trade repository must be reconciled against internal books monthly. Reporting errors must be corrected and resubmitted within 5 business days.

question: What are the requirements for managing risks associated with Payment Services Directive compliance?
ground_truth: Payment service providers must implement Strong Customer Authentication for remote electronic payments. SCA exemptions must be documented. Transaction monitoring must meet required fraud rate thresholds.
contexts: PSD2 Compliance Policy â€” Section 3.1: Payment service providers must apply Strong Customer Authentication combining at least two of the following: knowledge, possession, and inherence.

PSD2 Compliance Policy â€” Section 3.3: SCA exemptions must be applied only on the basis of a documented regulatory exemption subject to monitoring of associated fraud rates remaining below regulatory technical standard thresholds.

question: What are the requirements for managing the risk of greenwashing in ESG products?
ground_truth: ESG-labelled products must have documented investment criteria aligned with the stated ESG classification. ESG claims must be reviewed by Compliance before publication. Annual ESG performance reports must be published for each ESG product.

question: What are the requirements for managing open banking and API security risks?
ground_truth: Third-party providers must be registered with the relevant regulator and meet technical security standards to access open banking APIs. Customers must be able to revoke third-party access at any time. API security must be penetration tested annually.
contexts: Open Banking Risk Policy â€” Section 2.1: Third-party providers accessing customer data via open banking APIs must be registered with the relevant financial regulator and meet the firm's technical security requirements.

question: What are the requirements for managing risks in CBDC operations?
ground_truth: Participation in CBDC programmes requires regulatory approval and Board authorisation. CBDC holdings must be treated as central bank money for liquidity purposes. Technical integration must meet the central bank's API and security specifications.
contexts: CBDC Participation Policy â€” Section 1.1: The firm may only participate in CBDC programmes with regulatory approval and Board of Directors authorisation.

CBDC Participation Policy â€” Section 1.3: CBDC holdings shall be treated as central bank reserves and included in Level 1 HQLA. Technical integrations with CBDC infrastructure must comply with the central bank's API specifications and security requirements.

question: What are the requirements for managing the risk of climate-related stress testing?
ground_truth: Institutions must conduct annual climate stress tests over a minimum 10-year horizon covering transition and physical risk scenarios. Results must inform capital planning and be reported to the Board and supervisory authority.
contexts: Climate Stress Testing Policy â€” Section 2.1: Institutions must conduct climate stress tests at least annually incorporating both transition and physical risk scenarios over a forward-looking horizon of at least 10 years.

Climate Stress Testing Policy â€” Section 2.3: Climate stress test results must be used to inform capital planning decisions. Results must be presented to the Board and submitted to the supervisory authority as part of the annual supervisory reporting cycle.

question: What are the requirements for managing cross-border data transfer risks?
ground_truth: Personal data may only be transferred outside the EEA if the destination has an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards such as SCCs are in place. A transfer impact assessment must be completed before relying on SCCs.
contexts: Cross-Border Data Transfer Policy â€” Section 2.1: Personal data may only be transferred outside the EEA where the destination country has an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards including standard contractual clauses are in place.

Cross-Border Data Transfer Policy â€” Section 2.3: Before relying on standard contractual clauses, the firm must conduct a Transfer Impact Assessment evaluating the laws and practices of the destination country.

question: What are the requirements for managing the risk of inadequate financial promotions?
ground_truth: All financial promotions must be approved by an authorised person before issue, must be fair clear and not misleading, include past performance warnings where relevant, and approval records must be retained for three years.
contexts: Financial Promotions Policy — Section 2.1: All financial promotions must be approved by an appropriately authorised person before issue in accordance with applicable regulations.

Financial Promotions Policy — Section 2.3: Promotions must be fair, clear, and not misleading. Promotions referencing past performance must include a prominent past performance warning. Approval records must be retained for a minimum of three years.
